skill.name: landing-experience-checker
skill.description: Checks ad-to-landing-page continuity before launch. It reviews message match, above-the-fold offer and CTA, page speed evidence, form friction, and mobile rendering.
skill.summary: Preflight ad landing pages for message match, speed, form friction, and mobile experience.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline code, metadata URLs, and relative documentation links. One finding is confirmed: the skill instructs an agent to run a local Python connector against a user-provided landing URL, which should be guarded with validation and user confirmation.

remediation.issue: External connector command accepts a user-provided landing URL.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running the connector, validate http and https URLs, and pass the URL as an argument without shell interpolation.

remediation.issue: The skill references parent-directory documentation and sibling skills.
remediation.suggestion: Package required references with the skill or replace parent-directory links with marketplace-safe documentation links.

content.value_statement: Paid ads can fail when the landing page does not match the promise. This skill creates a launch-ready punch list for message match, speed, forms, and mobile rendering.
actual_capabilities: Compares ad headlines and hooks against the destination page promise.
Checks whether the offer and primary CTA appear above the fold.
Labels speed and mobile evidence as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Counts required form fields and names specific friction points.
Routes each failing check to the owning follow-up skill or workflow.
Produces a pass, partial, or fix punch list for launch review.
limitations: It does not rewrite landing page copy or redesign the layout.
It does not compute an account score or final go-live decision.
Speed and mobile checks need PageSpeed, CrUX, or rendered-page evidence for measured results.
It cannot verify continuity when both ad copy and page copy are unavailable.

use_cases.title: Pre-launch ad QA
use_cases.description: Review a campaign landing page before paid traffic starts and identify launch blockers.

use_cases.title: Quality Score diagnosis
use_cases.description: Find message, speed, form, or mobile issues that may hurt landing-page experience.

use_cases.title: Creative-to-page handoff
use_cases.description: Give page owners a focused punch list after new ad hooks or offers are approved.

prompt_templates.title: Basic landing preflight
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you have one URL and a small set of headlines.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check this landing page before launch: [URL]. Compare it with these ad headlines: [paste headlines].

prompt_templates.title: Quality Score preflight
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the page may affect ad relevance or landing-page experience.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Quality Score landing preflight on [URL]. Check message match, above-the-fold offer, speed, form friction, and mobile rendering.

prompt_templates.title: Measured speed review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when you can provide page speed or rendered-page evidence.
prompt_templates.prompt: Preflight [URL] with these ad hooks: [paste]. Use this PageSpeed or rendered-page export for measured speed and mobile checks: [paste].

prompt_templates.title: Advanced offer continuity audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when offer wording must match approved claims across ads and page content.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [URL] against these ads and approved offer terms: [paste]. Flag promise drift, unsupported claims, form friction, and the owning repair path.

output_examples.input: Preflight a webinar landing page against three paid search headlines.
output: Message match: Partial. The page repeats the webinar topic but omits the ad promise about templates.
Above the fold: Pass. The offer and primary CTA are visible without scrolling.
Form friction: Fix. The form asks for seven required fields, including two fields not needed for registration.

output_examples.input: Diagnose why a landing-page-experience rating may be below average.
output: Speed: Estimated. No PageSpeed export was provided, and the page appears heavy from visible assets.
Mobile render: Fix. The CTA is visible, but the form fields are cramped on a narrow viewport.
Next owner: Route copy and layout gaps to the landing optimization workflow.

output_examples.input: Check a promotion page against approved offer wording before launch.
output: Message match: Fix. The ad promises a limited-time discount, but the page only describes standard pricing.
Offer continuity: Fix. The live page wording does not match the approved offer terms.
Handoff: Reconcile offer wording before sending traffic.

best_practices: Provide the destination URL, ad copy, offer terms, and campaign goal together.
Label every speed and mobile observation as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Turn each failing check into one specific owner and repair path.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to redesign the landing page or write replacement copy.
Do not accept speed numbers unless they come from a measured or user-provided source.
Do not request a final account score or go-live decision from this skill.

faq.question: What does this skill check?
faq.answer: It checks message match, above-the-fold offer and CTA, speed evidence, form friction, and mobile rendering.

faq.question: Does it rewrite my landing page?
faq.answer: No. It identifies gaps and routes repairs to the proper follow-up workflow.

faq.question: Can it work without PageSpeed data?
faq.answer: Yes, but speed and mobile observations must be labeled as estimated unless measured evidence is provided.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the destination URL, ad headlines or hooks, approved offer wording, and campaign goal.

faq.question: Is it for paid search only?
faq.answer: No. It can check any paid campaign where ad promises must match a destination page.

faq.question: Does it make the launch decision?
faq.answer: No. It prepares the landing-page evidence for a separate account audit or launch gate.
